issues.legal_issue: A government may exempt an area from town-planning requirements when relevant circumstances make exemption expedient and it forms that opinion in good faith.
material_facts: The acquisition was for expanding an existing township, whose planned development had begun before the relevant planning legislation came into force.
The government cited rapid population growth, increasing housing demand, pressure for conversion of land, and the risk of haphazard development if expansion were delayed.
The government considered compliance with specified planning procedures impracticable in the circumstances and issued an exemption for the area to be developed.
The exemption itself was not challenged in the landowners’ writ petitions, and no factual foundation for invalidating it was laid there.
issues.conclusion: The exemption was valid; the circumstances stated in support of it were relevant to the statutory power, and the government committed no illegality in exercising that power.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 178(2) of the Punjab Regional and Town Planning and Development Act, 1995, the State may exempt a class of persons or an area from provisions of the Act where operation of those provisions would cause undue hardship or circumstances render exemption expedient. Expediency requires relevant objective circumstances and the government’s formation of an opinion on their basis; judicial interference is limited where the decision is not colourable or motivated by extraneous considerations. The Court relied on State of Gujarat v. Jamnadas G. Pabri, which distinguishes objective circumstances from the government’s subjective satisfaction, and Balbir Singh v. State of Haryana, which interprets expediency contextually and broadly.

rule.if: exemption_challenge_case and (relevant_urgent_circumstances and government_expediency_opinion) and not colourable_or_extraneous_exercise

predicates.exemption_challenge_case: A party challenges a government exemption from planning requirements in connection with a development-related land acquisition.
predicates.relevant_urgent_circumstances: Circumstances relevant to the exemption, such as pressing development needs and a risk of haphazard growth from delay, existed.
predicates.government_expediency_opinion: The government considered those circumstances and formed the opinion that granting the exemption was expedient.
predicates.colourable_or_extraneous_exercise: The government used the exemption power as a pretext or for an extraneous motive or consideration.

issues.definition: When a party challenges an area exemption, relevant urgent circumstances and the government’s expediency opinion support validity unless the exercise was colourable or extraneous.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition for expansion of an existing township is not invalid for failure to comply with planning requirements that have been validly exempted.
material_facts: The acquisition formed part of an expansion of an existing township rather than the establishment of a new town.
A notification had declared the township a local planning area under the planning legislation.
The government’s exemption from specified planning requirements was upheld.
The landowners did not challenge the acquisition on grounds based on non-compliance with the Land Acquisition Act.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was not invalid for non-compliance with the planning legislation because the exemption was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Once a valid exemption from specified planning requirements is upheld, acquisition cannot be struck down for failure to comply with those exempted requirements. The Court distinguished Sanjeet Singh’s case, which concerned a new township, a failure to comply with mandatory site-selection and planning-area procedures, and the absence of a validly selected site. It also relied on the distinction affirmed in Jasmer Singh’s case between a new town and expansion of an existing township.

rule.if: acquisition_challenge_case and valid_planning_exemption and existing_township_expansion and valid_planning_area_declaration

predicates.acquisition_challenge_case: A party challenges a compulsory land acquisition on the ground that planning requirements were not followed.
predicates.valid_planning_exemption: The government validly exempted the acquired area from the planning requirements said to have been omitted.
predicates.existing_township_expansion: The acquisition was for expanding an existing township rather than establishing a new town.
predicates.valid_planning_area_declaration: The relevant area had been declared a planning area through the prescribed process.

issues.definition: An acquisition challenge based on omitted planning requirements fails when the acquisition expands an existing township, the planning area was validly declared, and a valid exemption covers the omitted requirements.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of rehabilitation measures does not invalidate a compulsory acquisition made under law with provision for reasonable compensation.
material_facts: The property was acquired under validly enacted acquisition legislation.
The applicable law provided compensation based on market value, together with additional compensation, solatium, and interest.
Neither the constitutional property guarantee nor the acquisition legislation made rehabilitation a condition precedent to acquisition.
The landowners sought to rely on the absence of rehabilitation for owners dependent on acquired agricultural land.
issues.conclusion: The absence of rehabilitation measures did not make the acquisition legally invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 300-A permits deprivation of property by authority of law. Neither Article 300-A nor the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 makes rehabilitation a condition precedent to compulsory acquisition. New Reviera Coop Housing Society v. Special Land Acquisition Officer held that alternative sites may be provided by direction when the State proposes them, but are not a condition for every acquisition. Chameli Singh v. State of U.P. held that lawful acquisition for public purpose with compensation does not violate the right to livelihood merely because rehabilitation is absent.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_case and acquisition_authorized_by_law and reasonable_compensation_provided and not legal_rehabilitation_requirement

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns the compulsory acquisition of property.
predicates.acquisition_authorized_by_law: The property was taken under validly enacted law and in accordance with the applicable acquisition process.
predicates.reasonable_compensation_provided: The law provides compensation that reasonably accounts for the acquired property and the compulsory nature of the taking.
predicates.legal_rehabilitation_requirement: A constitutional or statutory rule makes rehabilitation a necessary condition of the acquisition.

issues.definition: For a lawful compulsory acquisition with reasonable compensation, the absence of rehabilitation does not invalidate the acquisition unless a legal rule makes rehabilitation necessary.

issues.legal_issue: A prospective land-pooling scheme cannot be imposed retrospectively on an acquisition and allocation process that has been completed.
material_facts: The land-pooling scheme was introduced prospectively and contemplated development arrangements that had to be planned as part of the acquisition process.
The acquisition and allotment process had already become final, and no provision for allocations to the owners had been made under the scheme.
Retrospective application could create confusion and litigation, and the record did not establish the area available for allocations in other sectors.
Applying the scheme only to the appellants could disadvantage owners who had accepted the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The land-pooling scheme could not be applied retrospectively to this completed acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: A land-pooling scheme that requires acquisition and allocation to be tailored from the outset cannot be mechanically applied after acquisition and allotment are complete. The Court considered the policy observations in Bondu Ramaswamy v. Bangalore Development Authority about ameliorative measures, but held that they did not justify retrospectively imposing this scheme on a finalized acquisition.

predicates.completed_acquisition_case: The acquisition and related allotment process had become final before the scheme was invoked.
predicates.prospective_rehabilitation_scheme: The government adopted the scheme for prospective application rather than for already completed acquisitions.
predicates.scheme_requires_advance_allocation_plann: The scheme requires allocation arrangements to be incorporated into the acquisition and development process from the outset.

issues.definition: A prospective scheme requiring advance allocation planning cannot be imposed retrospectively on an acquisition and allotment process that is already complete.

issues.legal_issue: Landowners may be permitted to seek a reference for higher compensation despite the expiry of the ordinary application period when the court orders that remedy in light of the pending litigation and the State’s position.
material_facts: The landowners had not applied for a reference to the civil court within the ordinary period.
The State did not oppose allowing them to apply for a reference despite the expiry of that period.
The State acknowledged that other owners had obtained references, and the landowners’ claims had been pursued in pending litigation.
The Court directed that applications made within the time it allowed be referred to the competent civil court for determination of compensation.
issues.conclusion: The landowners were allowed to apply for references within the period specified by the Court, and the Collector was directed to refer their claims for determination of compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides for reference of compensation claims to the civil court. In light of the State’s consent and the pending litigation, the Court granted a limited opportunity to seek that reference notwithstanding expiry of the ordinary application period.

rule.if: compensation_reference_case and ordinary_application_period_expired and state_does_not_object and pending_litigation_delayed_application

predicates.compensation_reference_case: The proceeding concerns a landowner’s request to have a compensation claim referred for civil-court determination.
predicates.ordinary_application_period_expired: The ordinary period for applying for a compensation reference had ended.
predicates.state_does_not_object: The State did not oppose permitting the landowner to seek a reference.
predicates.pending_litigation_delayed_application: The landowner’s challenge remained in litigation while the opportunity to seek a reference elapsed.

issues.definition: When the ordinary application period has expired during pending litigation and the State does not object, the court may allow the landowner to seek a compensation reference.
